mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the clock to the pineal gland was most worthwhile: the planned day–night comparison shows both increased nighttime melatonin and suppression by light.

leastWorthwhile.text: My first attempt was least worthwhile: adding the retinal cells directly to the body failed, although the cells were described as belonging to its existing eyes.

surprise.text: The outgoing pathway travels indirectly through the spinal cord and a nerve cluster in the neck before reaching the pineal location; that route was not intuitive to me.

arbitrary.text: The body could only be connected after building the pathway separately, despite already containing eyes and a brain. That assembly order felt somewhat arbitrary.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: tracing the distinct light-sensing pathway and its effects on a nighttime signal was interesting, though the final reference to several body-wide timing routes leaves their mechanisms unexplained.
